text:
maya_sales: Hey team — Astra Labs wants to run a 3-month POC with their custom astra-30b-utf8 variant. Requirements: p50 <120ms at 2k token context, KV-cache support, and FIPS KMS. They prefer managed but FIPS is a hard requirement. Can SE/Infra/security do a quick catalog + onboarding fit and pricing sketch?

jordan_se: Got it. Quick questions: is the variant q4_kv quantized? Any nonstandard tokenizer? I want to run a compatibility scan first.

maya_sales: Sales doc says "astra-30b-utf8-q4_kv". Tokenizer note: customer uses a slightly modified UTF-8 tokenizer that treats some unicode ligatures differently. They also shipped a small prompt corpus.

jordan_se: Ok. I'll run our local compatibility check:
```
redwood catalog check --model astra-30b --variant q4_kv --tokenizer astra-utf8
```
Expect checks: tokenizer mapping, kv-cache support, kernel compatibility for q4. If tokenizer differs we'll likely need a 10–20 line adapter mapping or a small pre-tokenize step.

ethan_infra: For the perf requirement (p50 <120ms @ 2k tokens): Hosted isn't viable with FIPS constraint. Dedicated in eu-west with 2 reserved A100-equivalent instances + prefix caching should meet P50 <120ms at low-mid concurrency. Notes: batching policy must be tuned (max-batch-size=8, batch-latency-slo=40ms).

ethan_infra: Rough cost sketch for 100k tokens/day:
- Hosted (no FIPS): ~$1.5k/mo (token billing) — doesn't meet FIPS
- Dedicated (eu-west, minimum reserve for perf + support): ~$5k/mo w/ POC discount and infra overhead
If they want FIPS-certified KMS + audit logs we need Private deployment or on-prem (customer-managed HSM). Dedicated does not currently include FIPS HSM out of the box.

lina_security: FIPS KMS = blocker for hosted. We need to confirm whether customer accepts Dedicated with customer-hosted HSM or requires a FIPS-certified HSM in our control plane. Also ask: data residency (EU?), retention windows, and whether they need deletion guarantees.

maya_sales: They flagged FIPS as mandatory and want EU residency. They'll accept Dedicated if we can provide audit logs and a dedicated VPC with their KMS in front. I'll confirm if on-prem is an option.

jordan_se: Compatibility check finished (local run):
- tokenizer: mismatch on bos/eos byte sequences — adapter required
- kv-cache: supported by our runtime (no changes)
- kernel: q4 path uses int8 opset, perf looks good on A100; no recompile needed
- estimated adapter work: ~3–5 dev hours + one test harness run

jordan_se: Sample adapter snippet I'll push to internal repo:
```python
# adapter: map ligatures -> normalized codepoints
def normalize_tokens(tokens):
    return [t.replace('\uFB01', 'fi').replace('\uFB02', 'fl') for t in tokens]
```

ethan_infra: Actionable infra items:
- I'll run a micro-benchmark on eu-west with the q4_kv image and the adapter once Jordan pushes it (ETA 24h).
- Prepare Dedicated sizing + pricing doc for POC (ETA 24h).

lina_security: I'll draft the security scoping note for the deal: will include FIPS implications, evidence we need for SOC2 + audit logs, and required SSO/SAML connectors for their SSO provider. ETA 48h.

maya_sales: Great — action list for sales follow-up: (1) I'll gather their prompt set + security contact + contract lead, (2) confirm EU residency is sufficient, (3) ask if they want on-prem fallback.

jordan_se: Plan: I'll open a short PR with adapter + tests and tag @ethan_infra for benching.

ethan_infra: I'll also note: if they want <100ms p50 we'll need extra headroom (3x the reserved baseline) — mention to customer.

maya_sales: Thanks all. Looping legal once security confirms. :+1:

deploy-bot: perf-bench job queued (job id: pb-78412) — will post results in this thread when finished.

maya_sales: I'll follow up with Astra and post their security contact and sample prompts here.
